about.title: Culver City Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Culver City sits at a busy crossroads of studios, residential neighborhoods, and heavy traffic corridors like Washington Boulevard, Sepulveda Boulevard, and I-405, where 80 injury collisions and 113 injured people were recorded in the most recent final year. Some of these crashes involve more than driver error — a defective airbag, faulty tire, failed seatbelt, or malfunctioning brake component can turn a routine trip into a serious injury. Beyond the roadway, Culver City residents also encounter defective household appliances, tools, children's products, and medical devices. California law allows injured people to pursue manufacturers, distributors, or retailers without needing to prove carelessness, which can make these claims different from a typical negligence case. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm, and we don't take a fee — we simply connect you with an independent attorney who can evaluate what happened and explain your options, working on contingency so there's no upfront cost to you.

whyChoose.title: Why Product Liability Cases Work Differently

items.title: Strict Liability Can Apply
items.desc: California generally allows injured people to hold a manufacturer responsible by showing the product was defective and caused harm, without having to prove the company was careless.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and even retailers along the supply chain can potentially be held liable, which may open more than one path toward accountability.

items.title: The Product Itself Matters
items.desc: Because strict liability claims often hinge on the physical defect, preserving the product — whether it's a car part, appliance, or consumer good — can be an important early step.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Under California's strict liability framework, you generally need to show the product was defective in design, manufacturing, or warning, and that the defect caused your injury. This differs from many other injury claims where negligence must be proven.

items.question: What if my injury happened in a car accident on Washington Boulevard or Sepulveda Boulevard?
items.answer: If a vehicle part like a tire, airbag, or brake system failed and contributed to the crash, that raises a separate product liability question alongside any driver-related issues. An independent attorney can look at police reports and vehicle evidence to sort out what role, if any, a defective part played.

items.question: What should I do with the product that injured me?
items.answer: Try to keep it in its post-incident condition and avoid repairs or disposal, since the physical product is often central evidence in these claims. Photos, packaging, and purchase records can also help an attorney evaluate the situation.

items.question: Is there a cost to get connected with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and attorneys in our network typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. We don't provide legal advice ourselves — we simply help connect you to someone who can.
